article_title: EduClaw-Bench: A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Pedagogical LLM Agents with Simulated Learners
citation: Lee, U.; Lee, S.; Jeong, Y.; Lee, E.; Shin, M.; Kwon, H. (2026). EduClaw-Bench: A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Pedagogical LLM Agents with Simulated Learners. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03206
title: KT-grounded simulated learner: coupling an AKT knowledge tracing model with LLM role-play for persistent simulated students
description: The simulated learner couples two components: a knowledge tracing model (AKT) that maintains a per-KC belief map trained on real student interaction data, and an LLM that role-plays the student and generates free-response attempts. The AKT model is "trained on real XES3G5M learners" and "maintains a per-KC belief map" that is updated at each observation. The LLM student generates answers conditioned on the KT belief state, and "graded probe outcomes are fed back into fθ, so KT and LLM stay coupled across D=30 virtual days." This design addresses the known failure of pure LLM-simulated students to reproduce real students' ability distributions, misconception dynamics, or authenticity under tutoring.
requirements: A KT model trained on real-student interaction data (XES3G5M elementary mathematics)
Persona seeds pooled from real training students' practice logs with precomputed initial beliefs
An LLM student whose system prompt is composed from ability level, grade band, and weakest/strongest KCs
constraints: The ability level is fixed at 'average' in all reported runs
Multi-seed confidence intervals are left to future work
examples: AKT trained on 5,027 sequences with test AUC of 0.80
2,169 persona seeds from real XES3G5M training students
ECE of 0.049 and Brier score of 0.033 over 1.19M item attempts
key_sources: Lee, U.; Lee, S.; Jeong, Y.; Lee, E.; Shin, M.; Kwon, H. (2026). EduClaw-Bench: A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Pedagogical LLM Agents with Simulated Learners. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03206

article_title: KT4EQG: Personalized Exercise Question Generation via Knowledge Tracing
citation: Xinyi Gao, Qiucheng Wu, Lu Ding, Q. Vera Liao, Kaizhi Qian, Ying Xu, Shiyu Chang, Yang Zhang. (2026). KT4EQG: Personalized Exercise Question Generation via Knowledge Tracing. Preprint. Under review. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23933
title: KT4EQG framework: knowledge-tracing-guided personalized question generation decomposed into education value and question-concept alignment
description: KT4EQG is a two-component framework for personalized educational question generation. A knowledge tracing model (KT2, a hidden Markov tree over a hierarchy of knowledge concepts) estimates each student's concept-level mastery and selects the KC with the highest education value, defined as "the potential improvement in the student's overall knowledge mastery after practicing". An LLM-based generator, trained via supervised fine-tuning then reinforcement learning with a learned alignment reward, produces a question grounded in the selected concept. The authors state that "KT4EQG decomposes the question evaluation into concept-level educational value and question-concept alignment value".
requirements: A knowledge tracing model providing posterior mastery probabilities per knowledge concept
KC annotations or a constructed KC tree for the target domain
A trained alignment verifier to supply the reinforcement learning reward
constraints: KT2 assumes each question is associated with one KC and correctness depends only on mastery of that KC
Experiments fix question difficulty to medium for KT-based evaluations
Evaluation is simulation-based, with student state updates assuming successful practice
target_learners: third grade mathematics students (per the generation prompt)
MOOC learners in wine knowledge, circuit design, and education theory modules
target_learning_goals: improving overall knowledge mastery across a domain's knowledge concepts
practicing the knowledge concept offering the greatest individual learning benefit
examples: On XES3G5M the framework generated a chicken-rabbit problem requiring reasoning over two entity types for the concept Multiple Quantities Chicken-Rabbit Problem
key_sources: Xinyi Gao, Qiucheng Wu, Lu Ding, Q. Vera Liao, Kaizhi Qian, Ying Xu, Shiyu Chang, Yang Zhang. (2026). KT4EQG: Personalized Exercise Question Generation via Knowledge Tracing. Preprint. Under review. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23933

article_title: KT4EQG: Personalized Exercise Question Generation via Knowledge Tracing
citation: Xinyi Gao, Qiucheng Wu, Lu Ding, Q. Vera Liao, Kaizhi Qian, Ying Xu, Shiyu Chang, Yang Zhang. (2026). KT4EQG: Personalized Exercise Question Generation via Knowledge Tracing. Preprint. Under review. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23933
title: KT4EQG system with released code
description: KT4EQG is an implemented personalized question generation system combining the KT2 knowledge tracer, a QWEN3-8B-based question generator trained with SFT and GRPO reinforcement learning, and an alignment verifier built on ALL-MINILM-L6-V2. The paper notes "Code available at https://github.com/UCSB-NLP-Chang/KT4EQG". The system was evaluated on XES3G5M and MOOCRADAR across six knowledge modules, with training on 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs and the verifier trained on a single RTX 3090 Ti.
requirements: Hierarchical KC annotations (expert-annotated for XES3G5M; LLM-constructed trees for MOOCRADAR)
A base LLM for generation and an embedding model backbone for the verifier
constraints: Experiments extend to 300 students per module for the three largest XES3G5M modules; smaller MOOCRADAR modules have 130-260 students
target_learning_goals: generating practice questions targeting each student's most beneficial knowledge concept
examples: The alignment verifier was trained for 70 epochs with batch size 64 and temperature 0.07, using sibling concepts from the KC tree as hard negatives
key_sources: Xinyi Gao, Qiucheng Wu, Lu Ding, Q. Vera Liao, Kaizhi Qian, Ying Xu, Shiyu Chang, Yang Zhang. (2026). KT4EQG: Personalized Exercise Question Generation via Knowledge Tracing. Preprint. Under review. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23933

article_title: Improving Palliative Care Knowledge of nurses caring for heart failure patients : Author and corresponding author.
citation: Ali Sana, McMillan Kim, Kelly Freya. (2025). Improving Palliative Care Knowledge of nurses caring for heart failure patients. BMC Palliative Care. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12904-025-01669-7
title: Knowledge-to-Action framework as the guiding structure for a nurse education quality improvement project
description: The project was guided by the action cycle of the Knowledge-to-Action framework, which the article describes as "involves identifying the problem, adapting knowledge to the local context, assessing barriers to knowledge use, selecting, tailoring, and implementing interventions, evaluating outcomes, and monitoring and sustaining knowledge use". The QIP operationalized this through stakeholder engagement, a literature search, semi-structured interviews, tailored hybrid sessions, and pre/post evaluation. Sessions were also designed based on Knowles's Adult Learning Theory principles, addressing gaps identified by learners to encourage self-directed learning.
requirements: Stakeholder engagement across project stages to adapt knowledge to the local context
constraints: Ongoing monitoring and evaluation of knowledge use were not possible because of the short duration of the QIP (eight weeks)
target_learners: Nurses caring for heart failure patients in tertiary cardiac care units
examples: Six-week implementation with in-person, virtual, and asynchronous participation options; each 40-minute session had a 20-minute didactic presentation, 10 minutes of case scenario videos, and 10 minutes of discussion
key_sources: Ali Sana, McMillan Kim, Kelly Freya. (2025). Improving Palliative Care Knowledge of nurses caring for heart failure patients. BMC Palliative Care. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12904-025-01669-7

article_title: Core competencies in the science and practice of knowledge translation: description of a Canadian strategic training initiative.
citation: Straus Sharon E, Brouwers Melissa, Johnson David, Lavis John N, Légaré France, Majumdar Sumit R, McKibbon K Ann, Sales Anne E, Stacey Dawn, Klein Gail, Grimshaw Jeremy, KT Canada Strategic Training Initiative in Health Research (STIHR). (2011). Core competencies in the science and practice of knowledge translation: description of a Canadian strategic training initiative. Implementation Science. https://doi.org/10.1186/1748-5908-6-127
title: KT Canada three-stream national training framework for knowledge translation capacity building
description: A national training framework organizing KT capacity building into three streams: Stream 1 for graduate and postdoctoral training in the science and practice of KT; Stream 2 for training in basic KT principles for researchers from other areas; and Stream 3 for basic training in the practice of KT for knowledge users. The authors state that "to enhance capacity we should focus training on three streams" covering science and practice of KT. The framework is guided by the MRC Framework for Complex Interventions and the Knowledge to Action loop, and includes core competencies, courses, seminars, a Summer Institute, and mentorship.
requirements: Funding and institutional partnerships (CIHR funding, eight participating universities)
Curriculum content anchored in the MRC Framework for Complex Interventions and the Knowledge to Action loop
constraints: The Knowledge to Action loop "may be less helpful for strategies targeting policy makers because many policy maker targeted interventions may focus on facilitating access to research in a timely fashion rather than supporting behavior change"
target_learners: Knowledge users including clinicians, healthcare managers, and policy makers
target_learning_goals: Skills in the science and practice of knowledge translation
Capacity to conduct syntheses and design, evaluate, and sustain KT interventions
examples: The Summer Institutes held 2009-2011 under themes such as 'Exploring the Knowledge to Action Framework' with 30, 29, and 31 attendees respectively
key_sources: Straus Sharon E, Brouwers Melissa, Johnson David, Lavis John N, Légaré France, Majumdar Sumit R, McKibbon K Ann, Sales Anne E, Stacey Dawn, Klein Gail, Grimshaw Jeremy, KT Canada Strategic Training Initiative in Health Research (STIHR). article_title: Core competencies in the science and practice of knowledge translation: description of a Canadian strategic training initiative.

(2011). Core competencies in the science and practice of knowledge translation: description of a Canadian strategic training initiative. Implementation Science. https://doi.org/10.1186/1748-5908-6-127
title: KT Canada Summer Institute with small-group project work, facilitated poster sessions, and mentor exposure
description: An annual event for graduate students focused on a different theme each year addressing one or more core KT competencies, such as developing KT interventions and targeting them to stakeholder groups. Institutes "include didactic and active learning with small group work focused on an assigned KT project and exposure to mentors" and facilitated poster sessions where trainees present research in progress. Three institutes were held with a total of 90 trainees (30 in 2009, 29 in 2010, 31 in 2011).
requirements: Invitation of graduate students; open to trainees without Stream 1 funding via a similar application process
target_learners: Graduate students and postdoctoral fellows in KT
target_learning_goals: Developing KT interventions and targeting them to different stakeholder groups
Presentation skills through facilitated poster sessions
examples: 2009 theme 'Exploring the Knowledge to Action Framework' (30 attendees); 2010 'Developing KT Interventions' (29); 2011 'Integrating the Science and Practice of KT' (31)

citation: Straus Sharon E, Brouwers Melissa, Johnson David, Lavis John N, Légaré France, Majumdar Sumit R, McKibbon K Ann, Sales Anne E, Stacey Dawn, Klein Gail, Grimshaw Jeremy, KT Canada Strategic Training Initiative in Health Research (STIHR). Implementation Science. https://doi.org/10.1186/1748-5908-6-127
title: KT Canada modular courses, e-seminar series, and online resources for KT training
description: The initiative delivers curriculum through modular courses in systematic reviews, pragmatic randomized trials, end-of-grant KT, and integrated KT; a monthly e-seminar series on KT research methodology with webcasts on the KT Canada website; a quarterly 'Research Operations' e-seminar for grant writing, manuscript preparation, and project management; and online modules and expert career interviews at ktclearinghouse.ca. Courses target audiences including trainees, researchers, physicians, and knowledge users, with 2011 offerings spanning evidence-based medicine, end-of-grant KT, systematic reviews, and pragmatic KT trials.
requirements: Technology (webcasts, online modules) to ensure national accessibility
target_learners: STIHR trainees, other trainees, researchers, physicians, knowledge users
target_learning_goals: KT research methodology, systematic reviews, pragmatic KT trials, end-of-grant and integrated KT
examples: 2011 course offerings included Introduction to Evidence Based Medicine (Winter 2011) and Pragmatic KT Trials (Summer 2011)
